title: AI and the Economy
text:
Imagine waking up with a notification that the exchange rate has increased, but have no idea why or how to react. For most of the people, it’s not like a hypothetical concept from a textbook, but a daily reality. According to the survey, over 57% percent of the respondents replied that they suffered inconvenience due to the exchange rate fluctuations, despite 53% of the respondents have never studied economics before. In this situation, AI makes daily life more complicated. While we always discuss about the ethical issues of AI, there’s another crucial point, we don’t trust what AI says. AI is like a huge black box so we cannot know where those informations are from. An article says ‘it is some deception of consumer selling some AI-generated contents.’ This quote illustrates the black box problem of AI. We don’t produce contents independently, so we don’t know how AI jumped to the conclusion. The real danger lies on the intersection of the asymmetry of information and the opacity of the algorithm. Therefore, government level regulation is no longer optional, but essential to ensure transparency and public trust in AI systems. Without certified standards, technological environment would undermine economic stability.
First, we must acknowledge that the economic crisis and technological risks share the same root, the lack of transparency. Out of 26 total survey participants, 23 were Korean nationals, and 15 were under the age of 30. The group also showed diverse major, including Economics, Tourism, engineering and nursing. The diversity of university major highlights that technological anxiety is the universal one. 11 respondents said that they are not that optimistic of both future economic society and AI usage. Even though 53% of the respondents haven’t studied about economics, more people feel anxious about the economic situation.
This opacity is more severe in AI usage. Most of the respondents said No when they are asked, ‘If an AI were to manage your personal finances, would you trust it to handle your money?’ The reason was mostly lack of trust and security concerns. Also, the interviewee who are majoring Anthropology said, “If you gave AI like and article to read or something, they’ll just like really dumb it down.”. These answers highlights a significant flaw of current AI systems. They prioritize simplified output over transparency. Consequently, it is clear that most of the people are still doubtful about the use of AI. However, we cannot simply abandon AI because we’re already living closely with AI. AI is everywhere, and its potential benefits to our lives are too huge to ignore. To have these benefits without risking ourselves, we need to make a fundamental root of pubic faith on the AI. This is why I suggest a proactive, national scale risk management system. Recently, the Un General Assembly unanimously adopted the global-scale resolution on AI, urging member states to protect personal data and monitoring Ai risks. This international movement proves that AI risks are no longer a personal concern, but a national responsibility.
One might argue that the corporations who deals with technology should be responsible for managing the risks which is mentioned above. However, relying solely on corporate self-regulation has a problem, which is a conflict between profit and protection. On the interview, when the interviewer asked the interviewee, ‘Do you think national regulation would undermine the AI industry’s competence?’ and the interviewee answered, ‘Since I do cultural anthropology, I ask a lot of questions about between cultures, and AI is kind of censoring itself.’, ‘I feel like it will stop people from having free speech or free will with AI and that will hinder its development.’ It is true that regulation partly hinders innovation. However, the absence of regulation can lead to far greater risks. Withoutclear standards, society will stay the same as now, lacking the faith that AI is responsible. Without clear standards, corporations will prioritize profits over transparency. Therefore, the regulation should be done in a government scale and the goal should not be a restriction, but as a safety fence in a more transparent direction. By establishing a clear standards when using AI, governments should gain more transparency in both area, economics and technology. To sum up, government can make AI regulations to make technological environment more sustainable, not harming economic status.
In conclusion, while AI keep shaping our society, especially economic environment, it is important to know that human judgements are still irreplaceable. As one interviewee pointed out, when AI summarizes the text given by a human, the overall quality decreases, which suggests humans are still better at even in trivial tasks. Another interviewee highlighted empathy, which highlights human giving meaningful insights to themselves. This highlights that AI should not completely replace AI, rather supporting human work. Therefore, an effective national risk management system should not focus only on regulation, but on collaboration between humans and AI. In a more concrete way, governments can make a law that urges corporations to clarity the sources of the AI generated contents. Also, providing education for people who was fired because of the AI job replacement could be also helpful. In conclusion, the goal is not to limit AI, but to ensure the synergy of collaborations in a way that prioritizes human values and strengthen public trust. By ensuring government-level standards and ensuring transparency, we can foster a sustainable technological environment which strengthens human value.

title: Generational Conflicts in Korea
text:
Generational conflicts in Korea are a hot button these days.  There are some aspects of generational conflict in Korea, like conflicts in office work due to the difference of thoughts. This TV program depicts generational conflicts in Korea, which mainly occur in the workplace, where diverse generations exist. Gen MZ is a newly coined word that means the group of people who are born in the late 1900s, and early 2000s. Generational conflicts occur everywhere, every time in the world and the main reason is the difference in values. However, what is special about the generational conflict in Korea is the historical background of each group and how the conflicting viewpoints of the two groups appeared. It is related to the Korean historical background. The author wants to figure out the differences in the social backgrounds of the two groups, compare them, and explain both side’s viewpoints. The goal that I want to accomplish through this essay is if someone in a particular age group reads my essay, I wish they could understand other age group’s viewpoints, therefore I need to explain both groups closely for that.
Generational conflicts and differences of viewpoints of two groups mostly appear in the workplace. The young generation prioritizes logic and rule, and the older generation prioritizes social values and customs.  Also, as a group member, they want to work alone and they want to improve themselves by doing group work.  For example, when there is a company dinner, Gen MZ thinks they don’t have to go have dinner if they don’t want to because they prioritize logic. However, the older generation doesn’t understand the reason why they are not attending the company dinner, which is the custom of the company. The reason why those values appeared is related to the historical or societal atmosphere of the two generations. Gen MZ has independent characteristics under the effect of media As the media develops, people interact with an unspecified number of people through the media rather than meeting and interacting with specific people  in person. This trend has made people less social, thus accelerating individualism, which focuses on the individual and himself rather than others..  The media made young people think alone at home with the media, so there are fewer chances to contact others.  When people who were born in the late 1900s~early 2000s were young, the media gradually began to spread. As the media spread, people became accustomed to communication methods using digital devices. Therefore, Generation MZ can freely express opinions without being bound to customs because they are familiar with digital communication methods, which is relatively free to make an opinion. (P. 278) In contrast, the gen baby boom, which is mostly the boss at work, grew up in a social atmosphere that faced the IMF, and several other economic crises. So, the social atmosphere at that time was based on overcoming the economic crisis together like a gold-collecting campaign in Korea. And their family had lots of kids so they naturally started to care about group, collaboration, and society. (Babyboom or bust: why South Korea is desperately trying to boost its birth rate, Charlotte Gifford (world finance)) With the difference in social background, there have been lots of differences in the two groups’ interests. Gen MZ’s independence and Gen Millennials’ interdependence clash, so these differences lead to other conflicts in other groups, like family, politics etc.
Therefore, efforts are needed to harmonize the interests of the two groups. Let me introduce some ways we can accomplish that harmony. First of all, setting a common goal can be helpful. We must set common goals, such as environmental protection and solving the problem of low birth rate, and make efforts together to achieve that goals. If we put our heads together, for example, environmental protection and try hard, harmony will form our society rather than generational conflict. In addition, events or education in which various generations can participate can be helpful. For example, cultural activities, technology exchange programs, and volunteer activities with youth and the elderly can be helpful, and it can be a place where several generations can unite as one.

title: Hypermarkets and Local Merchants
text:
If you have ever been to hypermarkets in Korea, you must know how many commodities there are. People always go to hypermarkets because all commodities are in them.  Even if you need tools, people go to hypermarkets. Also, if you need pork bellies, people go to hypermarkets. Any kind of item, people go to hypermarkets rather than local stores because they are big, comfortable, and have lots of commodities except what they need. In hypermarkets, they can not only purchase items but also go on eyeshopping, and it is quite interesting. Due to these reasons, local stores run by individuals are gradually losing power within the community. Hypermarkets are usually run by big companies but local markets are usually run by individuals, so if they lose power, they become very difficult to make a living. Due to this reason, there have been laws that regulate the mandatory closure of hypermarkets to protect traditional markets from the hypermarkets. Even though the hypermarkets closes on weekends, there are other means for hypermarkets, like online shopping, so small business owners are increasingly concerned, so they insist the legislation of mandatory closure days for hypermarkets. However, there have been voices that criticized the compulsory regulations of opening day and the violation of customer’s rights. From now on, they are arguing between the protection of traditional markets and the rights of customers. In more detail, as more and more hypermarkets appeared, in 2012, more small business owners tried to protect their markets but failed. Therefore, the law regulating the opening hours of hypermarkets appeared, but the other side, hypermarkets disagreed. (Loopholes in the abolition of mandatory closure of large discount stores, Lee Ji Won) They raised a petition to abolish the law that regulates their businesses. However, it was not accepted. As a result of the repetitive action, (the mandatory closing on weekends) law was abolished, now in 2024. (Abolish ‘Mandatory Holidays’ at supermarkets in Seoul, the passage of a city council, Kim Chae Bin, 2024)
In this situation, we should look for solutions for both sides to thrive. In the author's opinion, there should be some other means, not just regulating when and how to close. The goal is to protect local business, not violating customer’s rights. To accomplish that goal, the author's team thinks it will be helpful to minimize the mandatory holidays of hypermarkets, and come up with new ways to support small business owners. Author thinks that we need a measure of regulations on the economic system. Therefore, to accomplish that goal in such a situation, we need more means to protect local market businesses by creating conditions that would be more favorable to local merchants.
First, the government supporting local stores’ joint promotions and events to hold local specialties fair and local festivals so that local products can be sold would be helpful. About once a month, holding big events which can gather a large group of people and sell products which can be differentiated from hypermarkets can raise customer’s attention and it would be good for local businesses.
Second, creating a space for exhibiting and selling local products in hypermarkets would be helpful. In order to accomplish this event, the communication between hypermarkets and local markets is essential. If they communicate successfully, hypermarkets can help small business owners sell their products directly. In that case, the negotiations with hypermarkets like local business owners to minimize the number of closure days and adjust it to the situation of hypermarkets. However, creating a space for exhibiting and selling local products in hypermarkets will greatly help the development of the local economy and small business owners. By using this method, hypermarkets can strengthen the close relationships with society and strengthen cooperation with local businesses, and small business owners using facilities and infrastructure of hypermarkets to sell their products can be helpful for their businesses.
If it is possible, the author's idea can be helpful for both hypermarkets and local merchants in that it can boost each other’s business and also the local community.
The author hopes, with respect and care, the conflicts between large markets and local businesses will end peacefully in a way that takes care of all the interests of each other, and the author's opinion is convincing in that I think it would be beneficial to make both sides profitable rather than competing with each other. Also, promoting the consumption of goods will work more directly than any other method.

title: Language has contributed to the development of mankind.
text:
Language has contributed to the development of mankind. (from pragmatics point of view)
1. Language helps expand and preserve human thought and form community identity.
Language expresses and forms abstract concepts such as objects, concepts, and events, and generalizes abstract concepts to help humans understand the world. Knowledge expands with the help of language, becoming a common way of thinking or social knowledge of a group called 'culture' in our society. The way of thinking, lifestyle, and knowledge of culture remain through records and are passed down to the next generation, allowing the country to maintain its ancient tradition and survive. Cultural knowledge transmitted through language plays a major role in forming and conveying aesthetic, ethical, and social values in various fields such as art, history, tradition, and philosophy, thereby forming a common mindset within the community through language, preserving the specificity of the group, and enhancing humanity's diversity.
2. Language enables social interaction and allows individuals to feel a sense of belonging within society.
In the process of using language, humans interact to understand each other's intentions and attitudes. In pragmatic language research, individual language use is understood in context and situational context, which allows individuals to understand common or different language expressions within a community and learn to use appropriate language within the community. As a result, individuals go through the socialization process in the group and gradually become individuals belonging to the group. These interactions greatly help individuals feel a sense of belonging within society and form their identity by being part of the community.
3. Language is not limited to a single framework, so it allows for the creation of many things.
Language does not consist of a single algorithm. Many people improvise, communicate, and create their own languages. Based on linguist Chomsky, humans create language based on an algorithm called universal grammar. Therefore, language can continue to produce new content and change over time. This is why languages change and new words appear over generations in Korea, and it can be a reason for language to have variable characteristics.

title: Low birth rate in Korea; as the perspective of a university student
text:
According to this graph, there has been serious decrease of the average birth rate in Korea. From  1970, the birth rate is highly decreasing and now, in 2021, it has been recorded that a woman do not have a baby in average. This can be seem like a simple stastics, but it leads to sever social problems. When the low birth rate and aging problems becomes severe, there are problems like insufficient manpower and economic problem. These problems are all related to the economic problems like high house price, and the low economic development. There are also the jobs related to children, like teachers,’ demand decreases and this can lead to unemployment. Taken together, we can see that the population of young people is decreasing, but the socioeconomic burden and social responsibility are getting more and more severe. Therefore, it needs to be solved as soon as possible.
In order to solve this problem, we need to know the reason of this problem. This problem is deeply related to the social structure, so it seems that it is not easy to be solved, but knowing the reason can partly relieve this issue. The author conducted an investigation, targeted to university student. There has been 6 responses, and the respondents all knew about the low birth rate problem and they all knew the seriousness of this problem. Most of the university student actually felt the effect of low birth rate problem when they were living, like a decrease in the number of applicants for KSAT, and TO decrease of educational recruit exam. The university students including me thought that the reason of this social phenomenon is related to economic problem. Interestingly, the socioeconomic problem leaded to another economic problem. As the house price rises and unemployment getting worse and worse, the young generations felt burden for their own living so the marriage rate decreased, and also the birth rate decreased. This leaded to the loop and to some problems of the social structure of Korea, for example, the compulsiveness of the career break after the parental leave, and the lack of marriage due to the high living cost aggravated the problem.
Then, if my explanations, this problem is deeply related to the overall social structure of Korea, is right, the total resolve of the low birth rate problem is a really hard thing to achieve. Then, what can we do is to partly relieve this problem and trying not to make this problem getting worse. Let’s look the examples of the social problem one by one.
First, the women’s career break. For the baby, women should devote lots of time. But the need to devote lots of time and parental break make the women unble to do economic activity after parental break.
This table shows how severe the career break problem is thesedays.
To relieve this problem, first, we need some institutional arrangement to ensure women’s job after the parental break. However, this is not that easy because the corporations’ first goal is the pursuit of profit. So boosting telecommuting and implementing flexible work system could be helpful.
Second, high house price. This is the most hard problem, and need lots effort to be solved. The most fundamental problem is to lowering house price by rising interest rate but that’s not that easy to be achieved. Therefore, the comprehensive subsidy policies, such as childcare subsidies, house subsidies for the married couple will help.
And there are lots of more ways as a university student to do to relieve this problem. The educational volunteering for children, campaigns related to women’s professional rights, and political participation. What I want to say through this essay is the huge wave is needed to completely solve the problem, but relieving this problems are possible in many ways.

title: How can we get to the consensus? Examining the Struggle within Korea's Medical System
text:
These days, the issues about striking of doctors and medical schools are on the rise. It is due to the absence of consensus between government and the doctors. Both sides are protesting, and their arguments are too stubborn to make a consensus. Government is trying to increase maximum numbers of medical schools but doctors are opposed to that, so they are arguing by using means more than communications. To explain the situation of this problem, we should first look at the reason why government is trying to increase maximum numbers of the medical schools. It’s due to the problems of the K medical system.
First, it’s due to the lack of the numbers of doctors. Second is the unbalance of doctors. Some countries have few doctors although some big countries have lots of doctors. There are also some unbalances between departures, called avoidance of departure. The departure like cardiothoracic surgery and obstetrics departure has no or little doctors, so many patients are dying due to this reason. Therefore, the government decided to increase maximum numbers of medical school, and increase the absolute numbers of doctors.
However, doctors think that this is not the essential resolution to this problem. They said, according to the death rates of covid-19, it can be seen that Korea has a fairly excellent medical system, and it is because of the workload of Korean doctors, who have world-class skills. It was also possible because of the medical level of the assistants was so high that they were able to respond well be requesting assistants. However, it the number of the doctor is increased, they are doubtful whether new doctors can set the highest level of medical care or not. As the number of doctors are decreased, the ability to obtain from that workload decreases. Also, competition among practitioners in the metropolitan will also intensify due to the excessive discharge of doctors, and it can lead the more serious problems of the K medical system.
As a last resort, doctors decided to strike, which was a decision to show their strong will, but caused great confusion in Korea's medical system. The people who are in danger not being able to cured because of the absence of doctors is the most important and urgent problem of the striking of doctors, and we need to find resolution of this issue.
The author think that Korean medical system exists, and I agree that the imbalance of doctors is the real issue of K medical system. I saw on the news, it said there have been problems related to the lack of doctors in countryside. The news also said that they are trying to solve the problem by implementing a regional quota system but it did not worked well. But just increasing the number of doctors cannot be a solution. Before increasing maximum students of doctors, they have to solve the problems of medical system first, and if that problems is really because of the shortage of doctors, at then they have to increase doctors. However, even though I understand the doctors arguments and think that they worth doing the striking, author thinks striking is not a good idea. As a doctor, doctors have responsibility to save people’s lives and it must be the first thing for them, but I think it is wrong to neglect that duty and put the achievement of their goals first. They need to find other solutions for their protests, and that solution cannot be a striking.
